title: Answer to Question: A Meeting at the Deauville Resort in France with the Participation of France, Germany and Russia
text:
Answer to Question: A Meeting at the Deauville Resort in France with the Participation of France, Germany and Russia

Question:

Last week, specifically on 18 and 19/10/2010, a tripartite summit was held at the Deauville resort in France at the invitation of its president Sarkozy, in which German Chancellor Angela Merkel and Russian President Dmitry Medvedev took part beside him. Is this summit an initiative to form a new axis between France, Germany and Russia? And if so, what is its purpose? And what is its importance in the current international situation? Or is it an ordinary meeting, like any meeting between states to share some interests?

Answer:

1- Sarkozy called for this summit amid domestic and international circumstances:

As for the domestic, it is the unrest that is sweeping France in the wake of the issuing of the law on the so-called reform of the pension system...

As for the international circumstances, they are the more important, and they are manifested in the coming Lisbon conference on 19/11/2010, which will discuss the subject of the missile shield and nuclear weapons, and likewise the G20 summit that will be held on 11 and 12/11/2010 in South Korea, which will discuss the global financial situation that Sarkozy calls for reforming by creating a new global monetary system, in addition to the fact that France is preparing itself to take over the presidency of the G20 for a period of one year after its meeting on this date.

2- The importance of this summit lies in its being connected with the international situation, for it relates to the position of these major powers towards one another and towards the first state in the world, which is America. Although Germany is not a major power in the international situation, the attributes of a major power are present in it, besides the fact that it is a major power within the European Union.

It appeared as though Sarkozy was working to revive the France-Germany-Russia axis that was alive shortly before he and his two colleagues Merkel and Medvedev came to the seat of power in those states of theirs. Merkel and Medvedev also have an interest in this rapprochement, so they responded to their colleague Sarkozy. All three had a desire for this summit and hope to achieve interests for themselves. The French news agency (AFP) on 18/10/2010 reported "sources of the German delegation saying that among the most prominent aims of Merkel behind this summit is the file of European security, in addition to looking seriously at linking the Russian economy to the European economic machine." And it reported "sources of the Russian delegation that they see in the summit only the positive aspect of dealing with us as a European power that can be beneficial for Europe and for the world." This French agency added to its report, saying: "France has a small nuclear deterrent and fears that it will pay the price in the event of an Atlantic-Russian agreement on nuclear disarmament in Europe, especially since Britain has begun to give up its nuclear arsenal by not renewing it, while Berlin sees the missile shield as a positive step." The French agency added that the three leaders "agreed to work towards establishing a new partnership," and expressed "their satisfaction with the sincere and open talks and the goodwill, even regarding the subjects of disagreement between them." This indicates that these three states have interests that each of them wants to achieve by establishing a partnership between them.

3- These interests are as follows:

France sees that its nuclear weapons are targeted, and that there are American pressures on it, as happened at the Nuclear Security Summit held in Washington on 12 and 13/4/2010, where American President Obama called at the conference for Europe (and France in particular) to give up nuclear weapons and to make do with the missile shield system in their place. But France rejected the call to give up its nuclear weapons. Its president Sarkozy said at that time: "France will never give up this weapon unless it is certain that the world has become stable and safe" (13/4/2010, the American CBS television). So France sees that it is the one intended by that, and it does not want to give up its nuclear weapons, which it considers a source of strength and greatness for it. Sarkozy clarified this matter by saying: "This system (the missile shield system) can only be complementary to the nuclear deterrent, which France has no intention of giving up" (AFP 19/10/2010). France wants to strengthen itself with Germany and Russia so that they stand with it at the coming Lisbon conference, and adopt its opinion at the conference in confronting America, and prevent a Russian-American agreement on disarming Europe of nuclear weapons and having the missile shield take its place...

As for Germany, its voices have recently been raised to say that the missile shield is called upon to take the place of nuclear deterrence." The agency added: "However, Merkel was keen not to anger France when she said that any nuclear disarmament can only take place on the basis of the principle of reciprocity." So Germany supports nuclear disarmament, as it does not possess nuclear weapons and is prohibited from possessing them, so it does not agree with France on this point. However, Merkel wants other states among those that possess nuclear weapons to give them up, and not France alone or Europe alone, and the first one intended by her words is Russia. Germany saw that it is in its interest that Russia cooperate with NATO in order to keep its danger away, so Merkel said: "It is good news that Dmitry Medvedev agrees to take part in the NATO summit."

As for Russia, its position on the missile shield system is that it is not far from accepting it if America offers it enticements and reassures it that it is not targeting it. Medvedev stated in the wake of this tripartite summit: "Russia has not yet taken a decision on joining the unified European missile shield system," and he said: "We are now studying this idea, but I think that NATO itself must form a clear picture of Russia's participation in this system and understand what the result of joining would be, the agreements that could be concluded in this context, and the future of our cooperation." He stated that relations between Russia and NATO had been discussed at the Deauville summit and said: "I would like it that I will come to Lisbon to take part in the Russia-NATO summit that will be held on 20 November. It seems to me that this matter will help in finding compromise solutions and in developing the dialogue between Russia and NATO in general." (Russia Today 19/10/2010).

The Russian president hinted at his scepticism about the missile shield, and that he wants to understand what is intended by this missile shield, what its programme is, what the guarantees for Russia are, and what will be offered to Russia in return for that. Nevertheless, Russia at present does not want to stand in the face of America as happened in the time of that axis previously; rather, it is working to draw closer to America so that it restores its standing as a great power working to manage the affairs of the world beside America. So it flatters America at times and courts it at other times, so that it gives it that standing and makes it a partner in managing the affairs of the world, as it was in the era of the collapsed Soviet Union. It knows that Sarkozy's France and Merkel's Germany are incapable of standing in the face of America, and so it sees that it will not benefit much from forming a front with them in the face of America. It also knows that they are not sincere with it, for they are working to exploit it and make use of it.

5- It is not expected that France will succeed in reviving the France-Germany-Russia axis, because of the difference in aims and objectives:

Russia has not responded fully to France, which, together with Germany, has not met Russia's requests in a way that satisfies the latter. Their procrastination has appeared, and this procrastination was manifested in the subject of entry visas for Russian nationals to Europe. France wants to exploit Russia by drawing it to its side to stand in the face of America on the subject of nuclear weapons, since Russia possesses a large nuclear arsenal and does not think of giving it up; and the subject of the missile shield concerns Russia because it relates to it, and it is set up in its face.

As for France, Sarkozy wanted to find supporters for his idea of calling for the reform of the global monetary system that America controls, which means reconsidering the Bretton Woods Agreement concluded in 1944, which enabled America to control the economy of the world through the global financial institutions that were established in the wake of this agreement, such as the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, as well as making the dollar a world currency and a measure for gold and for the currencies of states. Sarkozy's call has been continuous since the global financial crisis reached its peak in 2008, but France has not been able to achieve it, because America stands in its face and because of France's inability to gather the states of the world behind it to achieve that.

France is working to strengthen itself with Germany and Russia to stand in the face of America on the subject of nuclear weapons and the missile shield, and likewise on the subject of reforming the global monetary system. However, this is not easy to achieve, because Russia has interests with America, and because Germany is not a nuclear state, besides the fact that it does not dare to cut its relations with the international economic institutions that America established.

Sarkozy also wanted domestically to strengthen his position before his people and the domestic political forces, so that he could press ahead with the approval of the law on reforming the pension system, which the French parliament approved today, 28-10-2010, after the Senate adopted it the day before yesterday, 26-10-2010, despite the unrest sweeping his country, by showing himself as doing great works for France, winning Germany and Russia to his side, and confronting dangers that France faces and wanting to save France from them. Germany and Russia realise that, and realise that France wants to lean on its meeting with them to solve its domestic problems.

As for the Germans, they want to continue sending their companies to Russia to invest and exploit there; indeed, they want Russia's doors to be opened wide for them so that they can do as they please, without the Russians obtaining the like in return. They likewise want to sell their goods to it, so that Russia's markets are opened wide to them, without the Russians coming to Europe, so that the Russians do not benefit from Western expertise and do not invest inside Europe, and Europe's doors remain closed in their faces. From the collapse of the Soviet Union until today, the Russians have not been able to come easily to Europe, since obstacles are placed in their faces and they do not obtain entry visas easily from the European embassies in Moscow. It is the European companies that go and invest there and export goods there. As for ordinary Russian traders, they obtain European goods such as cars by way of the Baltic republics such as Lithuania and Latvia, where they arrive and cannot go beyond them into the interior of Europe, because the nationals of these republics bordering Russia reach the heart of Europe, and especially Germany, and transport the goods to the Russians, because their states have been inside the European Union since 2004. Before this date there were great facilities for the nationals of these republics, ever since their separation from the Soviet Union, with the aim of annexing those states to the Union, and that has been achieved.

Accordingly, these political and economic (conflicts) between France, Germany and Russia make it difficult to establish this axis.

6- Therefore Germany and France held, beside this tripartite summit, a Franco-German summit parallel to the tripartite summit, and studied their common interests... A joint Franco-German statement was issued in which they asked for the Lisbon Treaty to be reconsidered from now until 2013, and asked for the establishment of "a permanent mechanism to provide organised handling of crises in the future, and to allow, in the event of a serious violation of the basic principles of the economic and monetary union... the suspension of the voting rights of the states concerned." So France and Germany adopt the European Union and want to preserve it with all the strength they have been given, and they want to strengthen the Union by economic openness towards Russia, but without integrating Russia economically with the European Union. Therefore the opinion of France and Germany on entry visas for Russians to the European Union was such that this opinion remained procrastinating over the abolition of visas, despite Medvedev's request for the abolition of visas again and again. Merkel's reply was to say: "We know that the subject of visas is an important subject for Russia, and we must advance step by step, because that does not happen all at once." As for Sarkozy, he answered saying: "Visas are an important subject for our Russian friends, so we will talk about it," and he added: "We have taken into consideration the request of President Medvedev, who has himself committed to other subjects," referring to the subject of energy, and he said: "There is no problem; we are trying to reach an understanding, and the important thing is that we make progress."

7- In summary, the Deauville summit was held by these three states, each of them aiming to achieve certain interests, some of them particular and some of them general, shared by these three states. Although it is not expected that the formation of a new, effective axis will result from this meeting, the mere fact of holding it is an influential step internationally, for for years the European states have not been able to meet apart from America to form an axis between them, even if only a theoretical one.
